memberdef.name: zkLockDataF2F

briefdescription.para: Lock up source (plaintext) data from a file and store the results (ciphertext) in a destination file.

detaileddescription.para:
This function encrypts and signs a block of plaintext data from a file and stores the result in a destination file.
The zymkey has two keys that can be used for locking/unlocking operations, designated as 'shared' and 'one-way'.
The one-way key is meant to lock up data only on the local host computer. Data encrypted using this key cannot be exported and deciphered anywhere else.
The shared key is meant for publishing data to other sources that have the capability to generate the shared key, such as the Zymbit cloud server.
ctx
(input) Zymkey context.
src_pt_filename
(input) The absolute path to the file where the source (plaintext) data is located.
dst_ct_filename
(input) The absolute path to the file where the destination (ciphertext) data should be deposited.
use_shared_key
(input) This parameter specifies which key will be used to used to lock the data up. A value of 'false' specifies that the Zymkey will use the one-way key whereas 'true' specifies that the shared key will be used. Specify 'true' for publishing data to another that has the shared key (e.g. Zymbit cloud) and 'False' when the data is meant to reside exclusively withing the host computer.
0 for success, less than 0 for failure.

C interface to Zymkey Application Utilities Library.

detaileddescription.para:
1.2.0
Zymbit Technologies, Inc.
This file contains the C API to the the Zymkey Application Utilities library, libzk_app_utils. Systems intending to run such applications require that the libzkapputils package be installed.

This API facilitates writing user space applications which use Zymkey to perform cryptographic operations, such as:
Signing of payloads using ECDSA
Verification of payloads that were signed using Zymkey
Exporting the public key that matches Zymkey's private key
"Locking" and "unlocking" data objects
Generating random data Additionally, there are functions for changing the i2c address (i2c units only), setting tap sensitivity and controlling the LED.

Developers wishing to build applications which utilize the libzk_app_utils library should additionally install the libzk_app_utils-dev package, which contains the necessary development files for the Zymkey's C library. To install this package on a system that does not need to run the applications (e.g. a Docker container or when cross compiling on a foreign architecture), use apt install --no-install-recommends libzkapputils-dev. This will prevent apt from installing the Zymkey's zkifc driver daemon.

Usage: #include <zymkey/zk_app_utils.h> To add libzk_app_utils as a dependency of a CMake-based project, add the following lines to your project's CMakeLists.txt file: find_package(zkAppUtils REQUIRED) target_link_libraries(target_name PRIVATE zkAppUtils::zk_app_utils) Makefile-based projects may likewise configure the library dependency via pkg-config: CFLAGS="$(pkg-config --cflags zkapputils)" LDFLAGS="$(pkg-config --libs zkapputils)"
